title: AI-Enabled Energy Systems: Technologies, Intelligence, and Security
description: AI-Enabled Energy Systems: Technologies, Intelligence, and Security is a one-day conference on October 28, 2026, in the Glass Pavilion on the Homewood campus in Baltimore, Maryland. The program covers emerging applications of AI across scientific discovery, energy and materials technologies, and infrastructure resilience. Invited talks from researchers in academia, industry, and government run through the morning, and an AI + Energy roadmap workshop follows in the afternoon, examining research priorities and opportunities for collaboration. The conference is hosted by the Data Science and AI Institute (DSAI) and the Ralph O'Connor Sustainable Energy Institute (ROSEI) at Johns Hopkins.

sessions.title: Research and Applications of AI in Buildings
sessions.description: Buildings are vitally important to our economy, energy systems, and daily lives. Nationally, the commercial sector accounts for nearly 20% of primary energy use, over a third of electricity use, and nearly $200B in annual energy expenditures. 17% of our GDP is attributed to the real estate and construction industries alone. As we enter the AI era, we are asking more of our buildings than ever before – that they operate as efficient cost centers, provide low-energy, comfortable indoor environments, and increasingly, be dynamically coordinated with the power grid. This talk will highlight current trends in the industry, and research on the potential for AI to advance building performance across the lifecycle. With a focus on software tools for the operational phase, Dr. Granderson will present recent findings on how AI is being used in today's commercial products and services. She will conclude with highlights of ongoing research underway at Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, spanning advances in AI-ready data infrastructure, autonomous control and operation, and robotics for inspection and maintenance.

title: Laboratory to Launchpad: Bringing Your Energy IP to Life
description: Laboratory to Launchpad: Bringing Your Energy IP to Life was a one-day conference held on June 11, 2026, at the Hopkins Bloomberg Center in Washington, D.C. The conference brought together faculty, students, postdocs, researchers, and other innovators interested in moving research toward application. Sessions covered commercialization, intellectual property, federal funding, startup formation, research communication, and other aspects of translating research beyond the laboratory. The conference was organized by the Energy Translation Steering Committee at Johns Hopkins (Corey Oses, Steven Cohen, Jonah Erlebacher, and Avi Bregman) with a Nexus Convening Grant from the Provost's Office, co-sponsored by the Carey Business School, the Whiting School of Engineering, and the Applied Physics Laboratory.

title: Quantum Computing in Practice: Hands On with Quantinuum
description: Quantum Computing in Practice: Hands On with Quantinuum was a two-day workshop on quantum computing and its applications across chemistry, physics, materials science, biology, engineering, data science, and artificial intelligence. The program included talks, discussions, research presentations, and hands-on tutorials using Quantinuum hardware and software.

title: Data-Driven Materials Modeling Workshop
description: The first Data-Driven Materials Modeling Workshop was held May 29–31, 2024, in Hodson Hall on the Homewood campus, sponsored by the Institute for Data-Intensive Engineering and Science (IDIES), the Ralph O'Connor Sustainable Energy Institute (ROSEI), and Advanced Research Computing at Hopkins (ARCH). Each day had a theme, a morning keynote and seminar, and a hands-on afternoon: high-throughput thermodynamic modeling, quantum chemistry and catalysis, and Monte Carlo and molecular dynamics. The seminars introduced data-driven approaches for experimental and computational materials research, and the hands-on sessions gave students experience implementing the methods with guidance from graduate students and postdoctoral researchers.
